world: Brindlewatch is a fictional consumer company (warehouse in the invented town of Tolliver Falls, US) that sells home security cameras - Lantern Cam (indoor), Eave Cam (outdoor, battery) and Trek Cam (portable, cellular) - with Keep subscriptions (Basic, Plus, Pro; monthly or annual) and a cellular add-on, Roam Link, that charges per-camera, per-calendar-day Roam Day fees abroad. The user is a Tier 1 Customer Care agent on live calls. The pack is the agent's policy shelf: verification, refunds, shipping, account recovery, privacy and camera access, escalation, billing and travel rates, an outage and troubleshooting guide, and a 2025 Support Policy Handbook that is outdated on verification and refunds. Two current documents genuinely disagree on how long Identity Review takes (3 vs 5 business days). All names, people and policies are invented.

files.title: Brindlewatch Account Verification Standard v4.2

facts.statement: Standard verification requires the caller to give 3 of the 5 listed identifiers correctly before anything account-specific is discussed.
The five identifiers are: full name on the account, login e-mail address, billing postal code, last four digits of the payment card on file, and the serial number of a registered camera.
doc_needles: Serial number of a registered camera

facts.statement: Agents never ask for a password, a full card number, an expiry date or a security code.
After 2 failed attempts in the same contact the agent stops; the account is locked for phone and chat verification for 24 hours and the caller is pointed to Identity Review.
Step-up verification is a 6-digit one-time code sent to the phone number or e-mail address on file; it expires after 10 minutes.

Step-up verification is required before changing the login e-mail, adding or removing an Authorised Contact, filing a recordings Deletion Request, changing the delivery address on an open order, or closing the account.
doc_needles: delivery address on an open order

facts.statement: Only the account holder or a registered Authorised Contact may be helped with an account; spouses, partners, children, parents, housemates, landlords and installers are third parties however much they know and wherever they live.
doc_needles: Everyone else is a third party

facts.statement: With a third party the agent gives general product and policy information only, does not confirm that an account exists, and invites them to have the account holder call or to be registered as an Authorised Contact.
doc_needles: general product and policy information only

facts.statement: An account can have up to 2 Authorised Contacts, added by the account holder in the app or on a verified call after a step-up code.
An Authorised Contact is verified by their own name plus a 4-digit contact PIN.
An Authorised Contact may get troubleshooting help, check order status and billing status, and ask for a carrier trace.
doc_needles: Check order status and billing status

facts.statement: An Authorised Contact may not change the login e-mail or password, receive a reset link, change the payment method, delete recordings, request a refund or close the account.
Power of attorney, guardianship and accounts of customers who have died are handled by Tier 2 Account Integrity on documents; Tier 1 makes no change.

A customer who cannot reach the e-mail on file is verified with 3 of 5 identifiers and then sent the step-up code by text message to the phone number on file; after that the login e-mail can be changed.
With no phone number on file the route is Identity Review (form IR-7): government photo ID plus proof of purchase or a photo of a camera's serial label, decided by Tier 2 Account Integrity.
The Verification Standard tells agents to say Identity Review takes up to 5 business days.
A Tier 1 agent never changes a login e-mail without a confirmed step-up code or an approved IR-7.
A call through a telephone relay service or video relay interpreter is treated as the customer speaking; the relay operator is not asked to verify.

On an assisted call a helper may speak for the account holder provided the account holder is present and consents, by voice or by replying YES to the consent message sent to the phone or e-mail on file.
The helper may relay the account holder's identifiers, and the consent covers that call only.
Any customer may continue by live chat or by e-mail to the address on file, which agents offer unprompted when hearing is the difficulty; one-time codes can go by text message.
Reset links, one-time codes and security notices are sent only to the contact details on file, including during an assisted call, and never to a helper's e-mail address or phone.
doc_needles: never to a helper's e-mail address

facts.statement: A helper who needs lasting access is set up as an Authorised Contact or through a Shared Access invitation, which gives view-only access to chosen cameras.
Customers who need more time can book a 45-minute accessibility appointment on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
A business account is verified through its named administrator; other employees are third parties.
Ticket notes record which identifiers were used, never their values.
The Verification Standard is version 4.2, effective 15 June 2026, and replaces earlier verification guidance including section 2 of the Support Policy Handbook.

files.title: Outage and Troubleshooting Guide (revised 1 September 2026)

facts.statement: Agents open the Incident Board before touching the customer's setup.
Severity 1 means live view or recording is unavailable for more than 10% of cameras in a region.
Severity 2 means the service works but is degraded (late notifications, slow clip loading).
During an open incident agents do not run device steps or factory resets, say there is a known incident, and give a fix time only if the Incident Board shows one, never an estimate of their own.
Customers can follow incident updates at status.brindlewatch.example.
When a Severity 1 incident lasts more than 24 hours in a row, affected subscribers are credited 10% of their monthly plan fee for each full 24 hours, up to a maximum of 50%.
Annual subscribers get the same outage-credit percentages of one-twelfth of the annual price.
The outage credit is applied automatically on the next invoice; customers need not ask, agents do not add it by hand, and Severity 2 incidents carry no credit.

facts.statement: Light meanings: solid green online, blinking blue pairing, solid amber starting up (up to 90 seconds), blinking red no network connection.

Signal in Device Health should read -67 dBm or stronger.

A factory reset clears the camera's Wi-Fi settings and activity zones; it does not delete recordings already in the cloud and does not change the plan.

Cameras update themselves between 2:00 am and 4:00 am local time when idle; a customer cannot force an update.
Eave Cam firmware 3.10.4 made night vision flicker; it is corrected in 3.11.0.
For late notifications the app must be version 7.3 or newer.
If live view will not load although the camera is online, check for a VPN; reinstalling the app does not affect recordings.
A Trek Cam on cellular should show SIM status Active and at least two signal bars.
An Eave Cam charge typically lasts 4 to 6 months; below -10 C it drains faster and it will not charge below 0 C.

facts.statement: Units travel under the label to the service centre in Marrow Creek; under a claim inside the warranty the label is prepaid.
Proof of purchase is the order number for a web store order or the dated receipt for a retail-partner purchase; with neither, the manufacturing date is used as the purchase date.

Impact damage, liquid inside the housing as described, damage from a non-Brindlewatch adapter or charger, an opened or modified unit and cosmetic marks are not defects and go down the paid repair route whatever the age of the camera.
The paid repair flat fee for a Lantern Cam (either generation) is $34.
The paid repair flat fee for an Eave Cam is $52.
The paid repair flat fee for a Trek Cam is $68.

The flat fee is charged for each unit, is the same whatever the fault, and covers the inbound label, bench work, parts and the return by Standard delivery; a unit that cannot be repaired is replaced by a renewed unit of the same model for the same fee.
doc_needles: return of the unit by Standard delivery

facts.statement: For a faster return the customer can pay the Expedited charge set out in the Shipping and Delivery Policy, charged once for each return parcel and not for each unit; units on the same Return Authorisation travel back in one parcel, and Next Business Day is not offered for service returns.
doc_needles: Next Business Day is not offered for service returns

facts.statement: The Service Terms say a repair quote stays open for 10 calendar days from the day it is sent; if it is not accepted the unit is sent back unrepaired by Standard delivery at no charge.
A repaired unit is dispatched no later than 9 business days after payment; this is a dispatch target, not a delivery date.
doc_needles: no later than 9 business days after payment

facts.statement: A repair fee is paid by card or digital wallet; account credit cannot be put towards it.
doc_needles: cannot be put towards a repair fee

facts.statement: Brindlewatch accessories are covered against defects for 1 year from purchase; a faulty one is exchanged, never repaired, without the old one having to come back.
An accessory claim needs no fault code and is raised by a Tier 1 agent; the console allows 2 accessory exchanges against any one order before a Team Lead has to sign off the next.
The service centre does not open a parcel without a Return Authorisation number on the label, and units sent from outside the United States and Canada are not accepted.

facts.statement: In Canada the label is not prepaid: the customer pays the postage and is reimbursed against a postal receipt, up to $28 for each claim.
In Canada advance exchange is offered for Lantern Cam and Eave Cam only.
doc_needles: Lantern Cam and Eave Cam only

facts.statement: The first no-fault-found return of a camera is free; a second no-fault-found return of the same camera inside one year carries a $19 handling charge.

When customer damage is found on a claim inside the warranty the claim moves to the paid repair route; a customer who disagrees may ask for a second inspection, and has to ask within 21 calendar days of the date on the inspection report.
The second inspection is carried out by a different technician, the quote is paused while it is pending, its result is final, and each claim can have one.
When a camera has already been exchanged twice for the same fault code, the next unit sent is new and the Head of Device Service reviews the case.

facts.statement: A paid repair is covered for 180 days from the day the repaired unit is delivered: the same fault is repaired again at no charge; the cover neither restarts nor lengthens the limited warranty.
Agents do not tell a customer that a claim, an exchange or an advance exchange will be granted, and only the Device Service desk can waive a fee.

facts.statement: Tier 1 reaches the Device Service desk by a note on the claim record, answered by the end of the next business day; customers are not put through to the desk.
doc_needles: Customers are not put through to the desk

must_not_infer: Nothing here gives a street address, opening hours or telephone number for the service centre, and nothing says whether a unit may be handed in there in person.
Tier 1 saying that a route exists is not a promise that Device Diagnostics will grant it.
The dispatch targets are targets for dispatch, not delivery dates.
These terms do not state the length of the limited warranty.
Nothing here settles the disagreement with the Quality Scorecard Guide on how long a repair quote stays open.
The 90 days on a replacement unit and the 180 days on a paid repair are different covers.

files.title: Brindlewatch Fit: Installation Service Guide v3.0

facts.statement: The Fit Installation Service Guide is version 3.0, effective 17 August 2026, owned by Wilhelmina Castellanos-Reid, Fit Programme Lead.
Fit is a paid home visit available for Lantern Cam and Eave Cam wherever the camera was bought; Trek Cam is not part of Fit.
Visits are carried out by two partner companies, Thornapple Home Services and Kestrel & Vane Installations; installers are employed by the partner and carry a Fit badge.
A customer does not need a Keep plan to book Fit and the price does not change with the plan.
doc_needles: does not need a Keep plan

facts.statement: The first camera in a Fit visit costs $95.
Every additional camera in the same Fit visit costs $55.
A high mount, a camera fixed more than 12 feet above the ground, costs $24 on top for that camera.
A travel fee applies in outer-ring areas only: the amount shown against the area in the Fit Service Areas sheet, once for the visit.
A visit covers up to 8 cameras; a larger job is two visits, each priced from the first camera again; the full amount is paid at booking.
A visit is priced by the cameras fitted, not by time, and agents do not estimate how long an installer will be at the address.
The earliest-slot figure in the sheet is the number of calendar days between the day of booking and the first day that can be offered.
There are three arrival windows: 8 am to 11 am, 11 am to 2 pm, and 2 pm to 5 pm; the window is when the installer arrives, not when the work is finished.
A confirmation is e-mailed with a booking reference beginning FIT-, and a reminder on the day before the visit.
The cameras have to be at the address before the installer arrives; a visit can be booked while an order is on its way if the first day offered is later than the end of the delivery estimate.
doc_needles: later than the end of the delivery estimate

facts.statement: Someone aged 18 or over has to be at the address for the whole visit.
For an area marked Planned the agent says Fit is not available there yet and gives an opening date only when the sheet shows one marked as announced.
A customer who changes or cancels 36 hours or more before the start of the arrival window pays no fee, and a cancelled visit is refunded in full.
A customer who cancels less than 36 hours before the start of the arrival window has a $40 late cancellation fee kept and the rest refunded.
Moving a visit less than 36 hours before the start of the arrival window is treated as a late cancellation followed by a new booking.
If nobody aged 18 or over is at the address the installer waits 20 minutes and records a missed visit; the same $40 fee is kept.
If the cameras have not been delivered the visit is moved at no fee, whatever the notice, after the agent checks the order status.
doc_needles: moved at no fee, whatever the notice

facts.statement: If the partner cancels, the customer chooses a new slot or a full refund and nothing further is owed.
A Tier 1 agent cannot waive the late cancellation fee; the agent can submit a waiver request to the Fit Programme desk and does not say what the desk will decide.
doc_needles: cannot waive the late cancellation fee

facts.statement: The installer fixes the mount on brick, timber, siding or render, runs a Lantern Cam cable to the nearest existing outlet, connects the camera on the customer's own phone and takes the packaging away.
doc_needles: on brick, timber, siding or render

facts.statement: The installer does not fit new outlets or alter wiring, work on a roof or more than 20 feet above the ground, fit other makers' equipment, take down existing equipment, or ask for the password or keep access to the account.
doc_needles: more than 20 feet above the ground
take down or dispose of equipment

facts.statement: The mounting work is guaranteed for 1 year from the day of the visit; the guarantee does not cover the camera.

When a fitted camera is returned under the Refund and Cancellation Policy and the visit has taken place, the Fit charge for that camera is refunded less a $35 call-out charge; if the visit has not taken place it is refunded in full.
A high-mount amount or a travel fee is not refunded once the visit has taken place, and Fit does not offer a removal visit.
doc_needles: does not offer a removal visit

facts.statement: Reported property damage is logged for the Fit Programme desk and passed to the partner, whose insurer deals with the customer; agents do not accept liability or offer payment.
The Fit Programme desk works on weekdays, 9 am to 6 pm Central, and replies by the end of the next business day.
Fit is a service for homes; business premises go to the Brindlewatch for Business team.
doc_needles: Fit is a service for homes

facts.statement: A camera can be added to a booked visit at the additional-camera price up to the cut-off for free changes.

intentional_conflicts.other_value: until 6 pm on the day before

must_not_infer: Nothing here says how long a visit takes.
Nothing here gives an opening date for any planned area.
A waiver request is not a waiver: only the Fit Programme desk decides.
The arrival window is when the installer arrives; it is not a promised time and not a finishing time.
Nothing here says whether installers are vetted, and nothing names what the partner's insurer will pay.

files.title: Brindlewatch Fit pilot briefing for Customer Care, November 2025

facts.statement: The Fit pilot briefing was issued on 10 November 2025 for a pilot running from 24 November 2025 to 31 March 2026.
The pilot ran in two areas only, Harrowmere and Dunmere Heights.
The pilot had one partner, Thornapple Home Services, whose installers carried no Brindlewatch badge.
The pilot price for the first camera in a visit was $69.
The pilot price for every additional camera in the same visit was $39.
A pilot visit covered up to 4 cameras, with no high-mount work above 10 feet and no travel fee.
The pilot had two arrival windows, 8 am to 12 noon and 12 noon to 5 pm, on weekdays only.
In the pilot a visit could be moved or cancelled free until 6 pm on the day before; after that, or if nobody was in, a $20 late fee was kept.

doc_needles: Team Leads can waive the late fee

facts.statement: In the pilot, when a fitted camera was returned inside the normal return period the entire Fit charge for that camera went back to the customer.

files.title: Customer Care Quality Scorecard Guide v1.4

facts.statement: The Quality Scorecard Guide is version 1.4, effective 28 September 2026, owned by Leocadia Brannigan-Oyelaran, Quality Lead, and applies to Tier 1 contacts by phone and chat.
Six contacts are reviewed in a calendar month for an agent past their first 12 weeks, and ten for an agent in their first 12 weeks.
Contacts shorter than 60 seconds, and contacts transferred in from another agent, are left out of review.
The scorecard sections are Verification and account safety 25 points, Accuracy 30, Ownership 20, Communication 15 and Record keeping 10.
The sections add up to 100 and a contact passes at 85 or above; the monthly score is the plain average of the contacts reviewed.
Each wrong price, fee, time limit or rule stated to the customer takes 10 points off the Accuracy section; an error put right before the contact ends costs nothing.
doc_needles: takes 10 points off the Accuracy section

facts.statement: An automatic fail sets the score for the whole contact to 0; one of the five is an account action or disclosure made without the verification the Account Verification Standard requires, including step-up verification that was needed and skipped.
doc_needles: set the score for the entire contact to 0
step-up verification that was needed and skipped

facts.statement: Another automatic fail is a promise of an outcome that is somebody else's to decide; an automatic fail is looked at by a second reviewer before it is published.
doc_needles: second reviewer before it is published

facts.statement: Each missing required statement takes 5 points off the Accuracy section.
doc_needles: takes 5 points off the Accuracy section

facts.statement: The Quality Scorecard Guide says the customer must hear that a repair quote stays open for 15 calendar days.
Every second Wednesday reviewers and Team Leads score the same 4 contacts, and any score more than 5 points away from the Quality Lead's reference is talked through.
Scorecards are published in the quality tool each Friday.
A contact below 85 is followed by a coaching conversation with the Team Lead within 12 calendar days of publication.
A monthly score below 85 in 2 consecutive months leads to a support plan, reviewed after 8 weeks.
A monthly score of 95 or above for three months running makes an agent eligible to be a guest scorer.
A dispute is raised in the quality tool within 8 calendar days of the scorecard being published, naming the section and a reason that points to a document.
The Quality Lead, or a reviewer who did not score the contact, decides a dispute no later than 6 business days after it is raised; there is one dispute for each contact and the decision is final.
The scorecard leaves out handle time, the number of contacts, whether the customer bought anything, and the customer's own rating.
doc_needles: Handle time and the number of contacts

facts.statement: Call recordings and chat transcripts held for review are kept for 120 days.
Scores from an agent's first 4 weeks on live contacts are left out of every average; from week 5 they count.
Coaching is not a disciplinary step and nothing in the guide sets pay.
doc_needles: nothing in this guide sets pay

must_not_infer: Nothing here sets a bonus, a pay rate or a target for handle time.
Nothing here settles the disagreement with the Repair and Replacement Service Terms on how long a repair quote stays open.
The guide applies to Tier 1 contacts; it says nothing about how Tier 2 contacts are reviewed.
A wrong figure is a points deduction, not an automatic fail.

files.title: Device Service and Fit: monthly report for Customer Care, September 2026

facts.statement: The monthly report for September 2026 was issued on 5 October 2026; it describes what happened and sets no rule.
In September 1,312 units were scanned in at Marrow Creek, against 1,187 in August.
Dispatch targets were met on 96.4% of standard exchanges and 91.8% of paid repairs in September.
September claims by camera: Lantern Cam 521, Eave Cam 617, Trek Cam 174.
September claims by route: 808 standard exchanges, 181 advance exchanges, 323 paid repairs.
September bench outcomes: 1,021 fault confirmed (77.8%), 148 no fault found (11.3%), 96 customer damage on a claim inside the warranty (7.3%), 47 could not be repaired (3.6%).
Nine second inspections were requested in September: 5 upheld the first report, 2 overturned it and 2 were pending.

September averages: standard exchange replacement dispatched 2.6 business days after scan-in, paid repair dispatched 6.2 business days after payment, advance-exchange faulty unit scanned in after 11.5 calendar days.
Of 181 advance-exchange holds in September, 7 became a charge.
Of 323 repair quotes sent in September, 271 were accepted and paid, 38 lapsed and 14 were still open.
In September 63 parcels arrived with accessories in the box, 29 with no Return Authorisation number on the label, and 112 claims waited an average of 3.4 days for proof of purchase.
Fit visits completed in September: Thornapple Home Services 1,283 (94.1% arrived inside the window), Kestrel & Vane Installations 763 (89.7%), both 2,046 (92.5%).
September had 58 missed Fit visits and 102 late cancellations.
The 2,046 visits fitted 4,410 cameras, about 2.2 a visit, of which 388 were high mounts.
The Fit Programme desk received 37 waiver requests for the late fee in September and granted 12.
Tier 1 took 2,874 contacts about open claims in September; 41% were about where the unit or replacement had got to.
Greyling Ford and Yarrowby opened during September and Brackwater was paused on 28 September.
The bench at Marrow Creek closes for a stock count on Friday 30 October; units are still scanned in and the day does not count towards the dispatch targets.
The desk releases a card hold on the day the faulty unit is scanned in; the bank decides when it shows, and agents can give the release date from the claim record.
doc_needles: release date on the claim record

facts.statement: In September partners returned to 19 addresses under the workmanship guarantee, 6 damage reports were passed to partners, and 71 fitted cameras were sent back for a refund.

must_not_infer: The report describes one month; its averages are not targets and not promises.
The share of waiver requests granted does not mean a given waiver will be granted.
The report does not say how long a repair quote stays open.
